title: CodeAnt AI Review Noise Controls: You Set the Bar for Every Review Comment
summary: Set the severity that reaches a pull request, fold nitpicks into one comment, stop repeat comments on new commits and teach CodeAnt AI your conventions.
body_markdown:
An AI reviewer that comments on everything gets skimmed. And when developers skim, the one comment that matters gets skimmed with the rest.


Today we’re launching **review noise controls** in **CodeAnt AI** . They decide which review comments reach your pull requests, including on the re-reviews that run after every new commit.


Here’s each control, one screen at a time.


## All your noise controls, on one page


Open Settings, then AI Code Review Configuration, and pick the organization or a repository. Changes save automatically.


The noise controls for payments-service, a repository of Northwind Labs, a fictional company.


## 1. Set the bar


The **Suggestion Threshold** is the minimum severity a finding needs to appear as a suggestion: Critical, Major or Minor.


Pick Critical, Major or Minor.


It covers every kind of finding, including typos, naming and docstring comments. Set it to Major, and pull requests get Major and Critical suggestions only.


## 2. Fold the small stuff into one comment


**Nitpicks** decides what happens to everything below the bar.


Nitpicks sits right under the threshold it works with.


Turn it on, and those suggestions go into one collapsed comment that developers open when they want to. Turn it off, and they aren’t posted at all.


Illustrative: one Major finding inline, and four minor ones folded into a single Nitpicks comment.


## 3. Keep re-reviews quiet


Every new commit is a chance for a reviewer to repeat itself. CodeAnt AI checks what it has already posted on the pull request and doesn’t post the same suggestion twice.


Choose how long CodeAnt AI waits after new commits before it reviews again.


The **Incremental PR Review Threshold** sets the wait, so a quick run of fix-up commits gets reviewed together. Reviews also check the base branch, so a bug that was already there isn’t blamed on the pull request that happened to touch it.


## 4. Close threads the fix already handled


Auto Resolve Suggestions, as described in the app.


Turn on **Auto Resolve Suggestions** , and each new commit resolves the CodeAnt AI comments it addresses. The threads left open are the ones still worth a look.


Illustrative: a commit adds the missing refund check, and CodeAnt AI resolves its own thread.


## 5. Teach it once


Every codebase has patterns that look wrong to an outsider. When a suggestion doesn’t fit yours, reply to it with` @codeant-ai` and the reason.


Illustrative: a developer explains why ledger writes stay uncaught, and CodeAnt AI saves it as a learning for src/ledger/**.


CodeAnt AI saves the reply as a **learning** , shows the files it applies to and stops flagging similar issues there. Every learning is listed under Settings, then Learnings, where your team can add, edit or delete them.


Northwind’s learnings for payments-service, each scoped by file pattern.


## 6. Narrow what gets reviewed


Security Only Reviews and the four exclusion settings.


**Security Only Reviews** limits suggestions, and their Nitpicks, to security issues. **Exclusions** keep review away from the files, source branches, destination branches and labels you choose, such as generated or vendored code.


## 7. Set it once for the org, adjust per repo


Every repository starts from the organization’s defaults.


Set the defaults once for the organization. Each repository inherits them or overrides a single setting, and overrides are labelled in the settings page. A payments service can show everything from Major up while a prototype shows Critical only.


### Why it matters


People only act on a reviewer they trust. Google’s static analysis team keeps checks that comment during code review under 10% effective false positives, because engineers ignore tools they don’t trust ([Communications of the ACM](https://cacm.acm.org/research/lessons-from-building-static-analysis-tools-at-google/) ).


AI review raises the stakes, because it can comment on every line. In an industry study presented at ICSE 2025, developers resolved 73.8% of an AI reviewer’s comments, but the average time to close a pull request rose from 5 hours 52 minutes to 8 hours 20 minutes ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.18531) ). And in Stack Overflow’s 2025 survey, 80% of developers used AI tools while trust in their accuracy fell to 29% ([Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.blog/2025/07/29/developers-remain-willing-but-reluctant-to-use-ai-the-2025-developer-survey-results-are-here/) ). Fewer, better comments are how an AI reviewer keeps its audience.


## Get started


Review noise controls are live now in CodeAnt AI.


1.


Open Settings, then AI Code Review Configuration.


2.


Pick the organization or a repository.


3.


Set the Suggestion Threshold, Nitpicks and Auto Resolve Suggestions.


4.


When a suggestion doesn’t fit, reply with` @codeant-ai` and the reason.


Read more about the[suggestions threshold](https://docs.codeant.ai/pull_request/customize/thresholds) ,[learnings](https://docs.codeant.ai/pull_request/features/learnings) and[security-only reviews](https://docs.codeant.ai/pull_request/features/code_review) .


*Northwind Labs and payments-service are fictional. The settings screenshots are from CodeAnt AI with Northwind example names. The pull request images are illustrations.*
